parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
A potential difference of 1.2 × 10^{3} V is applied between a pair of horizontal metal plates in a
vacuum, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
The separation of the plates is 3.6 cm. The electric field between the plates is uniform.
A particle of mass 5.9 × 10^{-6} kg and charge –4.2 × 10^{-9} C enters the field at point X with a
horizontal velocity of 0.75 m s^{-1} along a line midway between the two plates.
The particle is deflected by the field and hits the top plate at point Y.
parts.question_text_latex:
A potential difference of $1.2 \times 10^{3}\,\mathrm{V}$ is applied between a pair of horizontal metal plates in a
vacuum, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
The separation of the plates is 3.6 cm. The electric field between the plates is uniform.
A particle of mass $5.9 \times 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{kg}$ and charge –$4.2 \times 10^{-9}\,\mathrm{C}$ enters the field at point X with a
horizontal velocity of 0.75 m $s^{-1}$ along a line midway between the two plates.
The particle is deflected by the field and hits the top plate at point Y.
